summary: Jean Petitot is a philosopher and linguist who studied at the École Polytechnique from 1965 to 1968. He later held a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences around 1983 and directed at École Polytechnique from 1992 to 1999.

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at the University of Amsterdam under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, and later under John Marshall. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and directed at Leiden University (1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, and Édouard Chavannes. His posts included the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1913–1933) and Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean Varenne was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and studied under Jean Haudry. He taught Sanskrit at Aix-Marseille University (1962–1980) and Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (1981–1987).

Jean-Antoine Dubois was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the Collège de Bourg-Saint-Andéol and Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris. He served as director of the Seminary of Pondicherry (1813–1819) and later as supérieur of the Paris Foreign Missions Society in 1836.

Jean-Baptiste Biot worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École Polytechnique under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace, later holding professorships at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and the University of Paris from 1809.

Jean-Denis Lanjuinais was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who obtained a Doctor of Laws at the University of Rennes (~1768–1771). He served there as professor of canonic law in 1775 and joined the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1808.
Jean-François Desgranges was an Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1795 and was a student of Antoine-Léonard Chézy.

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Paris and also studied at the École du Louvre. He served as director of the Guimet Museum from 1986 to 2004.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris and Paris Nanterre University. His academic posts included Paris Nanterre University (1967–1970), Paris 8 University Vincennes-Saint-Denis (1972–1987), Emory University (~1993–1998), and the University of California, Irvine (~1987–1998).
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who studied at the Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, the Lycée du Parc, and the École Normale Supérieure, entering the latter in 1943.

Jean-Jacques Bochinger was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Strasbourg, Heidelberg University, and the University of Göttingen, as well as under Eugène Burnouf. In 1830, he served as a minister at the University of Strasbourg.

Jean-Jacques-Antoine Ampère was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Sorbonne (1830), the École Normale Supérieure (1830–1834), and served as professor of literature at the Collège de France (1833–1864).

Jean-Louis Burnouf worked in linguistics and related fields, studying under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held the chair of Latin eloquence at the Collège de France (1817–1844) and served as chief librarian at the University of Paris in 1840.

Jean-Luc Achard specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and was affiliated with the Centre national de la recherche scientifique, attested in 2003–2004.

Jean-Luc Chevillard is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli and T. V. Gopal Iyer. He has held positions at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique and Paris Diderot University.

Jean-Marie Casal was an archaeologist who studied at the Musée du Louvre under Philippe Stern. His career included posts at the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1951–1958) and as a research director at the National Centre for Scientific Research (1969–1975).

Jean-Michel Delire is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who completed his doctoral studies under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat. He has served as a lecturer on Indian science and Sanskrit texts at the Université libre de Bruxelles, attested from 2008 to 2025.

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and under Bernard Frank. He was a director of studies at the EPHE and professor at the Collège de France (2011–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a sinologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair for Chinese at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as president of the Bibliothèque nationale de France in 1832.
